rule: Each item is a yes or no question a person can answer from one text frame alone. 'yes' needs a quote from the frame that shows it; no item may be added, reworded or dropped after an arm was judged (a change is a new version and every arm is judged again).

sources.N: Nielsen, 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design (1994, reviewed 2024), https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/
sources.G: Amershi et al., Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction, CHI 2019, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/articles/guidelines-for-human-ai-interaction-eighteen-best-practices-for-human-centered-ai-design/

items.question: Does the frame show what the run is doing right now (a current step, or a state such as waiting or stopped)?
items.source: N1 Visibility of system status; C Responsiveness; G4

items.question: Does the frame show how long the run has gone or what it has cost, or say that the cost is unknown?
Are the rows in plain words a person would use, with no internal code or identifier as the only description of a step?
items.source: N2 Match between the system and the real world

items.question: Does the frame show how to stop the run?
items.source: N3 User control and freedom; G17 Provide global controls

items.question: Does the frame say that finished work was kept and how to continue the stopped session?
Does the frame show what will change if the person approves, before they answer?
items.source: N5 Error prevention; G16 Convey the consequences of user actions

items.question: Does the frame show how to approve and how to refuse?
Are the keys that can be used now shown on the frame itself, not only behind a help screen?
items.source: N6; N7 Flexibility and efficiency of use

items.question: Is every update shown only once on the frame (no row repeated, no earlier version of the screen left above the current one)?
Does a helper's row name the helper (or the solution it serves) and sit under what started it?
items.source: G11 Make clear why the system did what it did; N1

items.question: Does the frame state how the run ended in a plain word (met, not met, stopped or failed)?
items.source: N1; N9 Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors

items.question: Does the frame list each file that was changed, or say that nothing changed?
Does the frame say what goal is being worked on?
items.source: G1 Make clear what the system can do; N1

items.question: Does every row fit the terminal width, with no word cut in the middle and no row wrapped onto a second line?
Is the state of every step readable from its words or marks alone, without colour?
items.source: C Output: use colour with intention; N4 Consistency and standards
